scores.why: The ten-sheet structure holds, but sheets 9 and 10 contain approximately 653 and 456 presentation-layer words respectively, overwhelming the otherwise disciplined pacing.

fixes.quote: Six blocking open items from the brief:
fixes.change: Move this list into the existing open-items disclosure; retain one visible sentence identifying the unresolved scope and ingredient claims.

fixes.quote: Three corrections and one judgement call.
fixes.change: Present the corrections as three short annotations beside the affected draft excerpts, with the full explanation in the ledger.
Reduce each decision to action, accountable owner, deadline and release condition; keep the detailed measurement protocol and cost categories in the existing ledger.

scores.why: The product, evidence, usage, timing, risks and approval conditions are covered, but stakeholders lack the PRD’s transcript contingency and an embedded complete client deliverable.

fixes.quote: Weeks 2–3: two leads review three past projects each.
fixes.change: Add the PRD §8 contingency to the pilot ledger: confirm full-transcript availability in week 1; otherwise collect prospective kickoffs while retrospective work uses the remaining sources.

fixes.quote: Embedded extracts are shown here; complete source documents remain in the repository.
fixes.change: Embed the complete Greek and English briefs in optional disclosures so the standalone walkthrough lets a stakeholder inspect the actual deliverable.

scores.why: The AI/code/people distinction is explicit, but unexplained technical language and an inconsistent role legend create avoidable friction for nontechnical readers.

fixes.quote: one brief object, gaps as questions
fixes.change: Replace with “one structured brief, gaps as questions”; explain the JSON record only in the ledger.
Replace with “Write Greek + English” to make the output immediately understandable.
Use var(--red) so the icon visibly matches the accompanying “Red pen = people decide” label and later human annotations.

scores.why: The conditional recommendation leads and the evidence supports it, but repetition and a late return to the budget example weaken the closing decision sequence.

fixes.quote: This sheet is the summary. Sheet 02 is the product; sheets 03–09 the evidence; sheet 10 the decisions.
fixes.change: Remove this marginal paragraph because the executive-route links already provide the same orientation.

fixes.quote: The budget stays «κάπου στα ογδόντα»: no invented or resolved total in the brief or either render. Shadow Draft A invented one; the creative lead strikes it.
fixes.change: Remove this repeated example from the close; finish with the sponsor’s next action and the conditions required before week 1.

scores.why: Brief Builder has a clear promise, anatomy and human boundary, but its distinctive principles and practical operating handoff are more buried than a product story warrants.

fixes.quote: Ask, don’t guess · Surface, don’t resolve · Flag, don’t correct · Look up, don’t invent · Sign, don’t send
fixes.change: Promote a compact version of these principles from the ledger into the main product overview.

fixes.quote: Account lead records resolutions/signature in the brief object; creative lead evaluates.
fixes.change: State plainly that v1 requires a manual edit to brief.json and identify the proposed runbook as preparation for that handoff, making the actual operating burden visible.

scores.why: The serif editorial system, restrained palette and human red annotations are coherent, but the creative sheet’s narrow content column and delayed artwork weaken its hierarchy.

fixes.change: Add a desktop override for #ch09 .body to use the full grid width and give the creative evidence a deliberate text-and-art composition.
Place the principal artwork beside or immediately after the A/B propositions, ahead of the detailed brief and specification table.

scores.why: Spot-checks confirm the model IDs, 984,820 stage-one tokens, 1,134,734 total tokens, de-duplicated $3.55 cost, timings, 17 checks, quotations and recorded resolutions, with assumptions and known discrepancies appropriately disclosed.
The source provides self-contained assets, responsive layouts, focus treatment and modal keyboard handling, but read-all navigation state and the final mobile action need refinement.

fixes.change: Update the current sheet and navigation labels as the reader scrolls in read-all mode; currently scrolling only saves position, leaving Next and Back tied to the previously selected sheet.
Change the visible button label to “Start again” on the final sheet; on phones the destination title is hidden, leaving an unexplained “Next” that returns to sheet 1.

scores.why: The creative is honestly labelled and the artwork respects the core palette and claim restrictions, but the can crowds the wordmark and the acknowledged TikTok caption-zone collision remains unresolved.

fixes.change: Increase the gap between the yellow symbol and the product wordmark to at least one wordmark height; the current can visibly falls short of the brand’s clear-space requirement.

fixes.quote: 9:16 still frame at the TikTok in-feed spec; the lockup sits in TikTok’s caption zone, a dedicated 9:16 layout would raise it
fixes.change: Create the dedicated 9:16 composition now, raising the lockup and claim while retaining the mock-up label and provisional table-based specifications.

overall: Verified the required hash; no repository files changed. Strong evidence discipline, but the creative and closing sheets need tighter editing and hierarchy. Visual and UX scores are provisional: Chrome failed to launch, so assessment used the complete source and the inspected embedded can image.
